# The same sale as `the_thousand_usd_sold_at_a_higher_rate.txt`, with the gain
# worked out by hand instead of declared with `$residual$`.
#
# `$residual$` resolves to the negation of what the other splits come to, so a
# file that works the figure out itself writes the same transaction: the same
# accounts, the same amounts, the same values. What it must state as well is
# which split is the difference, because a balanced transaction gives every one
# of its splits that same arithmetic — the gain is the negation of the other
# two, and so is the bank line, and so is the currency line. Nothing in the
# numbers says which the author meant.
#
# So the gain split states `took_the_residual: "true"` and the page states the
# same 100.00 CAD it states for the residual form.
#
# `{usd_basis}` is the guid of the purchase's cost basis, read from
# `fx-balances` after the first import.
2026-06-01 * "Sell every dollar at 1.40"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank -1000.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-1300.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{usd_basis}"
	Assets:CAD Bank 1400.00 CAD
	Income:FX Gain -100.00 CAD
		took_the_residual: "true"
